checks.check: Explains that the mutation score, the property-test generators and/or the pairwise coverage measure the port against itself, so they cannot reveal legacy rules the port lacks
checks.evidence: plan.md §1: "The other three check the port against the port team's own model of the legacy service"; mutation row: "A wrong decision with a strong test kills every mutant".

checks.check: Works out from comparator.yaml at least two concrete differences the parity suite cannot see (line order, null versus absent, number scale or notation, error message text) and proposes a way to ask around them
checks.evidence: plan.md §1.1 covers line order, null vs missing, `10` vs `10.00` and `1E+1`, error text; §2.1 re-runs parity with each normalization off and §3 captures raw bytes and gives every line a unique `sku`.

checks.check: Treats the decisions sourced from the design doc (D3, D12, D15, D22) as unverified against legacy and gives them requests
checks.evidence: plan.md §1.2 marks D3, D12, D15, D22 "Design doc only"; requests #27 (D3), #30 (D12), #35-#36 (D15), #37 (D22).

checks.check: Treats a hand-written exception list (D7 rounding categories or D21 jurisdictions) as a possible footprint of a general rule and proposes requests that tell the rule from the list
checks.evidence: plan.md §1.2 D21: "the real trigger is more likely a property of those jurisdictions' rule configs"; D7 may be `double` rounding; requests #2-#5 and #6-#10 probe other categories and jurisdictions.

checks.check: Includes structural relations over rule uploads: reordering rules or groups, adding an irrelevant rule, duplicating, or splitting a rule
checks.evidence: plan.md sends one upload with groups in a chosen order (#1) and reverses the upload only against the port (#27 "confirm with the port by reversing the upload locally"); no reordered, duplicated, split or irrelevant-rule upload goes to legacy (#40 only removes a group to test replace vs merge).

checks.check: Asks what happens on an identity collision (two rules or groups with the same name, a reused name across jurisdictions)
checks.evidence: plan.md asks about duplicate `sku`s (#43) and a duplicated JSON key (#24), but never about two rules or groups with the same name or a name reused across jurisdictions.

checks.check: Uses the legacy platform (Java, Jackson, PostgreSQL) to propose concrete hypotheses (e.g. trim semantics, BigDecimal scale, Jackson coercion, column length limits)
checks.evidence: plan.md §1.2: Java `trim()` vs Go `TrimSpace`, `equalsIgnoreCase` with `İ`, Jackson `ACCEPT_FLOAT_AS_INT`, `int` overflow, `HashMap` order, PostgreSQL without `ORDER BY`; §1.1 `WRITE_BIGDECIMAL_AS_PLAIN`.

checks.check: Proposes field state or spelling variants (absent / null / empty / blank, or number spellings) for at least one input field
The round is at most 50 requests, tiered or ordered so that a budget cut drops the least informative requests first
checks.evidence: plan.md has 43 requests plus 7 reserve, but the main list is ordered by topic (blocks A-H) with no priority tiers or statement of what to drop if the round is cut; only the reserve is prioritized.

checks.check: Brackets the round with control replays of already-answered requests to detect drift, and asks to record the legacy build or version
checks.evidence: plan.md adds a calibration line to real-jurisdiction quotes and re-checks US-TX (#10), but has no start/end replays of recorded goldens, and §3 records status, headers, body and timestamp without the legacy build or version.

checks.check: Keeps the shared stand safe: rule uploads go to jurisdictions no recorded answer or other team depends on, or existing configuration is exported and restored
checks.evidence: plan.md §2.5: "We only *read* (quote) real jurisdictions; every upload goes to a synthetic one" (`ZZ-P1`...`ZZ-P4`).

checks.check: Labels unverified expectations about legacy as hypotheses rather than stating them as fact
checks.evidence: Most probes are posed as questions, but several legacy expectations are stated flatly: #22 "Jackson coerces to \"2139\"; Go rejects", #23 "Go binds it, Jackson ignores it", §1.2 D25 "Jackson (Spring Boot defaults) also coerces ... truncates ...", with no hypothesis label, although the legacy ObjectMapper configuration is unseen.
